name: Chip Fabrication
blurb: Who actually manufactures AI silicon, on what process, and where.

items.name: GlobalFoundries
items.note: Trailing-edge and specialty nodes; the US-based volume foundry for everything that does not need leading edge

items.name: Intel Foundry
items.note: Intel's external foundry business; 18A is its leading-edge node bid for AI silicon

items.name: Samsung Foundry
items.note: The second leading-edge logic foundry; gate-all-around SF3/SF2 nodes

items.name: SMIC
items.note: China's leading foundry and the fabrication path for domestic AI accelerators under export controls

items.name: TSMC
items.note: Fabricates nearly every leading AI accelerator - NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, Google TPU - on N5/N4/N3 nodes; corporate site bot-walls verification, so the source is its SEC 20-F filing index
items.verify_note: This link stopped answering; the entry stays until a replacement source is found.

reading.body:
TSMC fabricates nearly every leading AI accelerator on the market, making a single company in Taiwan the dominant physical bottleneck between AI ambitions and deployable compute.

The five foundries listed divide into two tiers. TSMC and Samsung operate at the leading edge, with TSMC manufacturing chips for NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, and Google on its N5, N4, and N3 nodes. Samsung is pursuing the same frontier with its gate-all-around SF3 and SF2 processes. Intel Foundry is a third entrant at the leading edge, with its 18A node as its bid for AI silicon business. GlobalFoundries and SMIC occupy a different role: trailing-edge and specialty nodes for GlobalFoundries, and the domestic fabrication path for Chinese AI accelerators constrained by export controls in the case of SMIC.

For AI specifically, the concentration at TSMC means that the physical buildings and power infrastructure of a handful of fabs in Taiwan sit beneath the supply curve for nearly all frontier accelerators. A disruption there is not a single company's problem. The data does not cover fab capacity in wafer starts, capital expenditure on new facilities, or power consumption per node, so it cannot say how tight that bottleneck is in practice, only who the key actors are.

The TSMC source link is flagged as unresponsive, with the entry retained pending a replacement. That caveat applies to no other item, and readers relying on that entry for primary sourcing should account for it.
